message.content:
Painting the entire exterior of the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking.  In practice, a professional crew would work in shifts, using scaffolding, rope‑access techniques and high‑pressure spray equipment.  A rough estimate for a full‑time crew (≈ 8 h/day) is:

| Surface | Approx. area | Paintable surface per hour | Hours needed | Days (8 h shift) |
|---------|--------------|----------------------------|--------------|------------------|
| Main lattice (steel) | ~ 30 000 m² | 200 m²/h | 150 h | ~ 19 days |
| Decorative elements | ~ 5 000 m² | 200 m²/h | 25 h | ~ 3 days |
| **Total** | | | **175 h** | **~ 22 days** |

So, under ideal conditions (clear weather, continuous work, no regulatory delays), you’re looking at roughly **three to four weeks** of continuous labor.  In reality, permitting, safety inspections, and weather interruptions could push that to **six to eight weeks** or longer.
